title: 9.6 Making Inferences from Experiments

icans: I can find the experimental difference of the means.
I can use resampling to test whether a treatment had an effect.
I can count the possible resamplings.

vocab: x̄(____________) − x̄(control), the difference of the sample means
the claim that the ____________ has no effect
shuffling all the data into new groups many times to see what ______________ happen by chance
ₙCᵣ ways to __________ which values go in one group

blocks.p: Shuffle all 10 cards, deal two piles of 5, and find the difference of the means. Repeat 5 times.
How many shuffles (yours and the class’s) gave a difference of 3 or more? __________  What does that suggest? ________________________

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

blocks.stem: The dot plot shows the results of an experiment. Find the experimental difference of the means. What does it mean?

notes: Resampling: If differences that large are _______________ when shuffled, reject the null hypothesis.

blocks.stem: The experiment in Example 1 was resampled 200 times. Only 6 of the 200 resampled differences were 2 or greater. Should you reject the hypothesis that the treatment has no effect?

notes: Number of resamplings: Ways to split n values into a group of r: _______________

blocks.stem: How many ways can the 14 values in Example 1 be divided into two groups of 7?
Is the experimental difference of the means positive or negative? Explain.
Control: 12, 15, 11, 14.  Treatment: 16, 18, 15, 19. Find the experimental difference of the means.
How many ways can 10 values be divided into two groups of 5?

tickets.stem: The treatment mean is 52 and the control mean is 47. Find the experimental difference.
In 100 resamplings, 45 differences were as large as the observed difference. What should you conclude?
How many ways can 8 values be divided into two groups of 4?
